name: Pastéis de Belém
seoTitle: Pastéis de Belém: Beat the Queue, Eat Them Warm
tagline: The original Belém custard tarts since 1837, 230 m from the Jerónimos Monastery and open every day

description.short: The original pastel de nata bakery in Belém: €1.60 each in 2026, the takeaway queue versus the rooms inside, and when to go.
description.full:
Pastéis de Belém is the bakery that has made the original Belém custard tart since 1837, from a recipe that came from the monks of the neighbouring Jerónimos Monastery. It sits on Rua de Belém about 230 m (3 minutes' walk) east of the monastery, so it slots in between sights rather than needing its own time block. It is open every day, including Mondays, from 08:00 to 21:00 (22:00 from July to September; 19:00 on 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January).

There are two ways to buy. The take-away counter at the front is where the queue on the pavement forms. The alternative is to go inside to the large tiled rooms at the back, which have table service; when the street queue is long, a table can be the quicker option, and it lets you eat the tarts warm. Queues are at their longest from late morning to mid-afternoon and at weekends.

A tart costs €1.60 and a box of six €9.60 on the 2026 menu. Cinnamon and icing sugar are provided to add yourself. A coffee is €1.20, and the menu also covers other pastries and savoury snacks such as croquetes and pastéis de bacalhau, so this can double as a cheap, quick lunch before heading back to the ship.

For a short call, the efficient order is Jerónimos first, tarts second, then either the Padrão dos Descobrimentos across the avenue (about 11 minutes' walk) or MAAT to the east (about 14 minutes). Belém railway station is about 9 minutes away on foot, and tram 15E runs along Rua de Belém. Boxes are easy to carry back on board, though the tarts are at their best eaten on the spot.
description.history: In the early 19th century a sugar-cane refinery with a small shop stood next to the Jerónimos Monastery. After the 1820 liberal revolution, the convents and monasteries were shut down in 1834 and the clergy expelled; someone from the monastery began selling sweet pastries in the shop to survive. Belém was then considered far from Lisbon and was reached mainly by steamboat, and visitors to the monastery and the tower took to the pastries. From 1837 they were baked in buildings attached to the refinery, following the monastery's recipe, which the bakery says is known only to the master confectioners who work in its 'secret room'.
description.significance: Pastel de nata is sold across Portugal and far beyond, but 'Pastéis de Belém' is this bakery's registered trade mark, and its tart remains the reference for the style. It is also the one Belém stop that needs no ticket and opens every day, which makes it a reliable anchor for a port-day plan, including on Mondays when the national monuments nearby are closed.

directions.general: Located on Rua de Belém in the historic Belém neighborhood, between Jerónimos Monastery and the waterfront
directions.fromCruisePort: About 7.3 km west, 200 m from the Jerónimos Monastery. Taxi 15-20 minutes, tram 15E from Praça do Comércio to the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos stop, or the train from Cais do Sodré to Belém and a 5-minute walk.
directions.publicTransport: Tram 15E from downtown to Belém stop (400m walk). Buses 727, 28, 729, 714, 751. Train to Belém station (10-minute walk).
directions.parking: Limited street parking nearby. Public parking at Praça do Império (5-minute walk).

seasonal.notes: Closes at 19:00 on 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January
Closes at 19:00 on 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January

admissionPrices.notes: Free entry. Pastel de Belém €1.60 each, box of six €9.60; coffee €1.20; other pastries from €1.70 (official 2026 menu).

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 10–20 minutes for take-away; 30–45 minutes sitting in
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Around opening (08:00) or in the evening. Weekday mornings are generally calmer than weekends.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Two options: the take-away counter at the front, or table service in the rooms inside. Add cinnamon and icing sugar yourself. Combine with the Jerónimos Monastery (3 minutes' walk) and the Padrão dos Descobrimentos.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2–2.5 hours return from the ship if you come only for the tarts; better as a 20–45 minute stop within a Belém visit
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: The take-away counter is at street level; the seated rooms may involve steps, so ask staff if you use a wheelchair. Reach Belém by taxi, tram 15E or train.
tips: Open every day from 08:00 until 21:00 (22:00 July–September), so it works before or after the monuments, or as the Monday plan when Jerónimos and the tower are closed.
If the pavement queue is long, go inside and ask for a table in the seated rooms at the back rather than waiting at the take-away counter.
2026 menu prices: €1.60 per tart, €9.60 for a box of six, coffee (café) €1.20.
Cinnamon and icing sugar are provided; add them yourself while the tart is still warm.
Fit it between sights: the Jerónimos Monastery is 230 m west, the Padrão dos Descobrimentos about 11 minutes' walk.
Queues are longest from late morning to mid-afternoon and at weekends; opening time and the evening are generally calmer.
Savoury snacks from €1.70 (croquetes, pastéis de bacalhau €1.90) make it a quick lunch stop.
Belém railway station is about 9 minutes' walk, and tram 15E runs along Rua de Belém past the door.

highlights: Original Pastéis de Belém® made to the 1837 recipe, €1.60 each
Tarts made by hand on site every day
Tiled seated rooms behind the take-away counter, with table service
Other pastries and savouries: travesseiros, queques, croquetes, pastéis de bacalhau
Boxes of six (€9.60) for taking back on board

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Take-away counter at street level. Some of the historic seated rooms may involve steps; ask staff for assistance.
